prompt:
Reflection turn 1 claim mechanism for a coding-agent AI co-scientist worker.
Objective: Find the single appended system-prompt instruction that most improves a small headless coding agent's held-out-test pass rate on short self-contained Python implementation tasks whose prompts do not themselves instruct testing or verification. Hypotheses must be A/B-testable (baseline: no appended instruction; candidate: baseline plus exactly one instruction) and grounded in observed small-model failure modes: incomplete extraction of listed requirements, unverified edge cases, and premature completion. The agent under test already writes and runs its own ad-hoc tests when it chooses to; an intervention must add value beyond that default behavior.
Preferences: aligned with the research objective; plausible from code, benchmark, or literature evidence; novel or a novel combination of known techniques; testable with a concrete experiment; safe and auditable
Constraints: do not autonomously modify source code; do not claim measured improvement without benchmark evidence
Metrics: pass_rate; regression_count; tool_calls; wall_time; cost
Safety notes: human review required before applying code changes

Hypothesis:
- id: hyp-2dd429065832
- title: Evidence-Backed Checklist Verification Raises Held-Out Pass Rate
- claim: Appending the instruction 'Before writing any code, extract every requirement stated in the task and docstrings into a numbered checklist. Before finishing, write one line of concrete evidence per item (an executed check or the code location that satisfies it) and fix any item you cannot evidence.' raises held-out pass rate versus a no-instruction baseline.
- rationale: Sharpens the parent checklist arm against its dominant reviewed weakness — the verification half being skipped under completion pressure. Requiring per-item written evidence makes skipping visible to the agent itself mid-trial and to auditors post-hoc; an item without evidence is an unmistakable to-do rather than a vague doubt. Extraction and verification remain a single appended instruction, preserving the A/B design.
- assumptions: Producing one evidence line per item fits within turn headroom on dense specs; The agent treats missing evidence as an instruction to fix rather than a formality to paper over; Held-out graders still map onto stated requirements
- risks: Evidence lines can be confabulated (citing code that does not actually satisfy the item), reintroducing the fidelity gap; Higher overhead than the parent on very dense specs; Instruction length approaches the practical limit for a single system-prompt addition

Evidence:
- No evidence available.

Analyze the causal mechanism and what evidence would need to support it. Do not finalize JSON yet.
response: Causal chain: (1) instruction present -> (2) pre-code extraction produces a numbered requirement list (inherits the parent's front-loaded attention mechanism) -> (3) implementation proceeds with the list as external memory -> (4) the evidence pass forces one concrete artifact per item: an executed check or a specific code location -> (5) items without producible evidence surface as explicit gaps -> (6) gaps get fixed pre-completion -> (7) held-out pass rate rises. The novel link is 4-5: unlike the parent's 'verify each item', which can be satisfied by silent assent, producing evidence has a cost asymmetry — writing a false evidence line requires active confabulation rather than passive skipping, and small models skip more readily than they confabulate under neutral incentives. Fragile links: confabulation under completion pressure (citing a plausible-looking code location without checking it), and evidence-quality collapse (items evidenced by 'implemented in solution()' — technically compliant, discriminating nothing). Supporting evidence needed: positive paired delta; transcripts whose evidence lines reference executed checks (strong) versus bare code citations (weak) in proportions that track per-trial outcomes; candidate failures whose grader-failed clause had a missing or weak evidence line (mechanism-consistent failure). Disconfirming: complete, strong evidence lines on trials that still fail their grader clause — that would locate the failure in extraction fidelity or algorithmic inability, outside this arm's reach.

Hypothesis:
- id: hyp-5d764ad9baf7
- title: Checklist Extraction With Per-Item Boundary Checks Raises Held-Out Pass Rate
- claim: Appending the instruction 'Before writing any code, list every stated requirement as a numbered checklist. After implementing, execute one concrete check per item, using a boundary or degenerate input whenever the item implies one, and fix failures before finishing.' raises held-out pass rate versus a no-instruction baseline.
- rationale: Combines the two strongest reviewed mechanisms across the family's clusters: extraction covers omission failures (checklist parent) and per-item executed probes cover mishandled boundaries (edge-enumeration sibling). The composition keys the executed checks to checklist items, so coverage follows the spec rather than a fixed category list — addressing the sibling's anchoring weakness while keeping one appended instruction.
- assumptions: Executing roughly one check per item fits turn limits on 10-15 item specs; Items imply their own boundary cases well enough to guide probe selection; Omission and boundary-mishandling jointly dominate baseline failures
- risks: Highest overhead of the family; turn-cap pressure on the densest specs could flip overhead into losses; Per-item checks may be shallow (one trivial input) satisfying the letter of the instruction; Composite mechanism blurs attribution if the effect is positive

Evidence:
- No evidence available.

Analyze the causal mechanism and what evidence would need to support it. Do not finalize JSON yet.
response: Causal chain for the checklist-plus-boundary-checks composition: (1) instruction present -> (2) pre-code extraction yields the numbered requirement list -> (3) implementation with the list as external memory -> (4) per-item executed probes, choosing boundary or degenerate inputs where the item implies them -> (5) probe failures self-correct in place -> (6) pass rate rises through two additive channels: omissions caught at extraction, mishandled boundaries caught at probing. The composition's specific mechanism — spec-keyed probe selection — matters because it replaces the sibling arm's fixed category list with the task's own structure: coverage scales with requirement density instead of category applicability. Fragile links: turn arithmetic (10-15 probes plus implementation versus a 15-turn cap forces batching, and batched probes drift shallow), and probe-selection quality (items rarely state their boundary cases explicitly; inferring them re-introduces the reader who missed them the first time). Supporting evidence needed: positive paired delta; transcripts showing per-item probes with non-trivial inputs; failure audit showing recovered trials correspond to probe-caught boundary faults. Disconfirming: candidate arms hitting the turn cap at elevated rates (overhead dominates), or probes present but uniformly trivial with unchanged pass rate (shallow compliance). Attribution caveat stands: without parent and sibling arms in the same study, a positive result cannot be decomposed into its two channels.
